people.name: Ilya Shirokov
people.intro:
Hey all, I am Ilya, and I am nearly finished with my PhD in geometry and topology (St. Petersburg Department
of Steklov Mathematical Institute). We generalized Hopf’s theorem, and now we can say that if two travelers start at antipodal points on Earth, they can meet under the condition that, along their paths and to arbitrarily high accuracy, the temperature and pressure will be the same (as long as these functions are continuous). I believe I will work on topology while also developing my research in AI Safety in parallel.

The magic of high-dimensional spaces in LLMs and the mystery of how they work really attracted me, and about a year ago I started research in AI Safety. At first it was mostly a theoretical dive into existing methods and techniques in Mechanistic Interpretability. Later, together with a friend, we wrote two posts (1 and 2) about hidden reasoning in small LLMs (spoiler: it seems that there is none). To better understand the full picture, we developed a method for analyzing information flow in attention layers in terms of SAE features (no post about this yet). I am very excited to apply this to the study of unfaithfulness and see what comes out.

If anyone knows of interesting geometric effects or observations in LLMs, please let me know — I’d love to discuss. So far I haven’t found a good way to apply topology. I am based in St. Petersburg, but in Junary might be in London for a month.

My general research interest is to develop models that facilitate learning in a manner more aligned with human cognition and I am particularly focused on demonstrating the advantages of such models for reinforcement learning settings.

I'm currently on the lookout for PhD opportunities across Europe in the field of Neuro-AI. In the mean time, I've also developed a deep interest in AI safety and alignment recently and to this end I'll be working with Christopher Ackerman on "Understanding Self-Awareness in LLMs." Hoping to get further into AI safety in the near future. Very excited to connect with you all!

In my free time, I love to go indoor bouldering, DJ, and watch a lot of movies!

During SPAR I will be working with Alex Cloud and team on gradient routing.

You can find out more about my work at my website: https://mclarke1991.github.io/ and happy to connect on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-alan-clarke/.
